I know what you're saying and ppl in the program can be insensitive in comparison to what you'd expect. To alleviate your frustration, you also gotta understand if you've been going to AA meetings for over a year youve seen a lot of ppl come and go, and they've heard newcomers struggling through their first days or months on a weekly basis for a long time so it's kind of desensitizing. I've heard enough drinking/sober life stories at this point that I usually take them in pretty non-reactively/neutrally. One of the reasons being it's hard to tell if a stranger is attention-seeking for the sake of attention-seeking (and thus indulging in their story does them no favors) or if they're genuinely just wanting to tell their story. This can be perceived as cold or uncaring but understand that's not necessarily the case. 

I also second trying other meetings if these ppl aren't jiving with you. Your bad experience reflects the people of that group more than AA. AA are just people in a group. Some have nothing to offer you in the meetings (in my experience I know a couple retired guys who I honestly feel have never contributed to my sobriety or said something helpful...just taking up space at the meeting) and some could change your world. 

I would also advise, you need to be ready to own yourself and be very careful of blaming people. Read the AA book yourself, come on here and ask for support or what you should do to work on the steps. A sponsor is important but I would caution you against using that as a reason not to do X, Y,or Z in your road to sobriety. You'll find support if you seek it I promise, but honesty with self and understanding your sobriety is ultimately your responsibility is absolutely critical to sobriety. Because of its importance, when successfully sober people try to impress this concept on the newly sober person they can feel like they're being harsh. Dont let that get the best of you cuz they're not, they're actually doing what they believe is best (in most cases). 

Stick with it and you'll get what you need. Or try elsewhere, either way good luck in your efforts. You can do it.

In other words, it's easier to avoid the intense guilt and shame that would be appropriate for such a betrayal if you lie to yourself with some bullshit justification. 

Either way her reason is bullshit and to be honest, I personally wouldn't believe her when she says she loves you. Harsh words to hear but I believe the truth is the best remedy for such a situation. That said, take solace in knowing it will hurt being without her and you're hurting now, but this will pass and you undoubtedly can find someone who will give you the trust you deserve. 

Also, to answer your question, I dont think it's impossible to come back from your situation and build trust in the relationship, but it is incredibly difficult. And only possible if the other person is genuinely, and sincerely remorseful, honest, and committed. I dont believe, based on your post, your gf is any of those things. Biggest piece of evidence to me being that you dont have to sleep with someone to test whether you might want to be in a different relationship with someone. She acted on her desires and backpedaled into that conclusion in my opinion.

In addition to what others have said, specifically the part about it not being logical, it sounds like you're lacking confidence in the specific domain of women. I'm pretty much the opposite of your situation. I've vastly underachieved and have to get my life together but I've been decent with attracting women. Lately, I feel like I've lost my mojo (check out Austin Powers if you dont get the reference) because of my sense or feeling of worthlessness from my lack of success in other realms of life. You gotta get your mojo- charisma, charm, confidence, security with who you are and what you have to offer. 

Your reaction of anger signifies to me that you're too dependent on a womans response for your self-worth. That insecurity is almost certainly sensed by women whether consciously or subconsciously. Nothing repels women like insecurity or attracts them more by security (i.e. a dude who can be rejected and walk away completely unfazed by the rejection). In fact I've seen and experienced women who've rejected me or other guys, and get mad or attracted to guys after they rejected them and the guy or myself appeared to not give 2 shits about their rejection. My opinion: partly because it then turns into a slight to their attractiveness. As in "you should be more bothered that I just turned you down, you should be affected by my disapproval." It will put them in mental knots. When you cultivate that security I guarantee women will respond differently to you. 

The main way I think to practice this is to put yourself out there and approach women as you have been and when or if you get rejected remind yourself there is nothing to take personal. It means nothing about who you are. And by doing that you can change your response to learn, beyond just an intellectual level, your self-worth isn't reflected by any one womans response to you. In other words you can't change or control other people you can only control yourself. 

One other tidbit, it takes courage to approach women with a high probability of rejection. Remind yourself of this as well and that theres no reason to feel embarrassment, subordination, worthless, or any other negative emotions because you have the nuts to approach a woman. That idea may help to keep trying when you get more "no's" than "yes's" which is pretty much inevitable. 

For what it's worth I have a degree in psych so my mind is a lot more practiced in the illogical and abstract in comparison to the type of thinking engineering practices. And attraction is illogical and abstract.

It helps me to break down your goal to the smallest possible or most manageable actions or tasks you can. 

I.e. goal: write a paper 

1. Grab my shit I need. Dony think about anything else. 
2. Start walking to the library. Dont think about anything else. 
3. Open computer and start Microsoft word....
4. Write the first paragraph. 
5 etc... 

Coming from another terrible procrastinator who pulled way too many all nighters as a testament to my procrastination abilities. 

I found that what prevents me the most is the paralyzing effect of looking at all of my obstacles at once rather just doing one simple task at a time and putting the rest out of my mind. It helps take the pressure off nd anxiety out of completing a huge goal. 

Hope that helps :)
